text:
mira: quick sync 1: we're splitting the control plane for private deployments (regional cp inside customer VPC) and i want to call out heartbeat/lease design and peering failover tradeoffs. high level question: how aggressive can leases be before we risk flapping during transient peering blips?

tom: main concern is false-positives on agent liveness. if TTL too low we churn reconnections and re-auth handshakes. i'd keep lease >= 45s for WAN peering, use keepalives at ~15s. for internal LAN/cross-AZ tenants we can be 10s/3s.

jess: we should decouple control-heartbeat from data-path health. control TTLs are about orchestration; data flows should use their own probe and fallback. otherwise a short cp heartbeat will yank routes while flows still healthy.

ed: checklist items:
- leader election window: jitter the renew to avoid stampedes
- backoff on re-register to avoid route thrash
- metric `cp_lease_renew_latency` and alert at p95 > 200ms

mira: suggestion: two-tier liveness: a fast "soft" lease for UI/metrics (10s) and a slower "hard" lease for routing decisions (60s). UI can show agent down quickly while routing holds for safe time. thoughts?

tom: that works. UI-level soft lease can be optimistic. routing should only react on sustained hard-lease expiry or explicit decommission command.

jess: also consider a short grace period after failover where we keep old peering announced for 5m with lower priority. helps webhooks/whitelists and long TCP sessions.

ed: perf note: more aggressive leases increase API server load. need to scale controlplane reconcile QPS or use push-based heartbeats (agent pushes state) instead of polling.

mira: config draft (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
control: 
  soft_lease_seconds: 10
  hard_lease_seconds: 60
  renew_jitter_percent: 20
  backoff_seconds: 2
  max_backoff_seconds: 120
routing:
  post_failover_hold_seconds: 300
  announce_priority_decrease: true
```

jess: ops-bot can we add a canary that validates this pattern? steps: 1) provision regional cp in test-vpc 2) set soft/hard leases 3) simulate 10s peering blackhole 4) assert routing not flapped and metrics tracked.

ops-bot: canary job created: cp-lease-canary-2026-01-10. will run every 6h. link: https://ci.internal/canaries/cp-lease-canary-2026-01-10

ed: also need to document cert rotation semantics across peered cp instances. don't auto-rotate at same second across peers. rotate with overlapping validity window + staged trust anchor switch. otherwise clients see short-lived TLS failures.

mira: good call. add to runbook: rotate->validate->promote pattern with per-peer delay of 60s.

tom: final ask: dashboard panels for: lease expiry rate, hard vs soft lease discrepancies, route-flap count per-tenant, tcp session resets around failover window. alert if route-flap > 5/min per region.

jess: i'll add Grafana dashboard and link to RFC draft. Mira, want me to include the two-tier lease YAML in the RFC?

mira: yes please. i'll include the canary runbook and the cert rotation sequence. thanks all. :+1:

deploy-bot: noted. schedule maintenance window draft: 2026-01-11 03:00-05:00 UTC. please review canary results before approving.

mira: will do. posting RFC soon.
